gaps.sentence: Heavy snow made the mountain road ___ (PASS).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: impossible to travel through (im- + -able)
gaps.explanation: Heavy snow blocks the road, so the negative adjective 'impassable' (im- + pass + -able) is needed.

gaps.sentence: Mozart was the greatest ___ (MUSIC) of his age.
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ian forms the person: music becomes musician.

gaps.sentence: The treaty will strengthen economic ___ between the two countries (COOPERATE).
gaps.explanation: An adjective is followed by a noun: cooperation (-tion noun).

gaps.sentence: It was the most ___ (FORGET) trip of my life.
gaps.hint: negative adjective: too good to forget
gaps.explanation: 'Unforgettable' = impossible to forget; 'forgetful' describes a person who forgets.

gaps.sentence: The thunderstorm was absolutely ___ , so the children hid under the blankets (TERRIFY).
gaps.hint: the storm causes the fear (-ing); note 'terrific' means excellent
gaps.explanation: The storm causes terror, so it is terrifying; the children felt terrified. 'Terrific' means excellent.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (INVENT) of the new engine worked day and night.
gaps.explanation: The person who worked day and night is the inventor; 'invention' is the thing created.

gaps.sentence: She has been a loyal ___ (EMPLOY) of the firm for twenty years.
gaps.hint: person needed: someone who works for the firm
gaps.explanation: An employee works for a company; 'employment' is the uncountable state of having a job.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (ARRIVE) of the train was announced.
gaps.explanation: The subject must be a noun: arrival (-al noun of 'arrive').
